data.title: 5-Fluorouracil (injection + topical)
data.body:
_Injectables · V Immunosuppressants_

**Class:** Pyrimidine analogue antimetabolite (antineoplastic)

## Mechanism of action
- Converted to fluorodeoxyuridine monophosphate, which inhibits thymidylate synthase → no thymidine → no DNA synthesis
- Also incorporated into RNA
- In keloids: inhibits fibroblast proliferation and TGF-β-driven collagen production

## Pharmacokinetics
- IL use gives minimal systemic levels; systemic drug is metabolised by dihydropyrimidine dehydrogenase (DPD)

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- Intralesional: keloids and hypertrophic scars (alone or mixed with triamcinolone), warts, keratoacanthoma, small BCC (selected)
- Vitiligo (with microneedling/dermabrasion, off-label)
- Topical 5% cream for actinic keratosis, Bowen disease, superficial BCC (topicals slot)

## Dose & formulations
- Supplied as 50 mg/mL injection
- Keloids: 50 mg/mL alone, or mixed with triamcinolone (e.g. 0.9 mL 5-FU + 0.1 mL triamcinolone 40 mg/mL); 0.2–0.5 mL per cm² of lesion; total usually under 2–3 mL per session; every 1–4 weeks
- Keratoacanthoma: 50 mg/mL, 0.1–1 mL weekly

## Adverse effects
- IL: pain, burning, ulceration, purpura, hyperpigmentation
- Systemic (rare with IL): myelosuppression, mucositis, diarrhoea; severe toxicity in DPD deficiency
- Systemic 5-FU skin effects: hand–foot syndrome, serpentine supravenous hyperpigmentation, photosensitivity

## Contraindications
- Pregnancy and breastfeeding
- Known DPD deficiency; bone marrow suppression; infection at site

## Drug interactions
- Warfarin effect increases
- Sorivudine/brivudine (antivirals): fatal DPD inhibition

## Monitoring
- CBC if large or frequent doses are used

## Pregnancy & lactation
Contraindicated (old FDA category D/X depending on form).

## Viva points
- Thymidylate synthase inhibitor
- 5-FU + TAC combination for keloids reduces atrophy and recurrence
- DPD deficiency → severe toxicity
- Supravenous serpentine hyperpigmentation with IV use

## Topical form: Topical 5-fluorouracil (5%, 0.5%)
_Topical antimetabolite (5% cream; 0.5% cream; 4% cream)_

**Mechanism**
- Thymidylate synthase inhibition in rapidly proliferating dysplastic cells

**Indications**
- Actinic keratoses (field therapy), Bowen disease, superficial BCC (5%), warts (off-label, under occlusion), vitiligo (after dermabrasion — off-label), disseminated superficial actinic porokeratosis

**Dose & how to apply**
- AK: 5% twice daily for 2–4 weeks (or 0.5% once daily); sBCC/Bowen: twice daily for 3–6 weeks

**Adverse effects**
- Intense inflammation, erosion and crusting (expected), photosensitivity, pigmentary change; toxicity in DPD deficiency (rare)

**Contraindications**
- Pregnancy; DPD deficiency

**Pregnancy:** Contraindicated.

**Viva points**
- Field therapy for AK; inflammation is expected; combine with calcipotriol for better effect

_Sources: Wolverton 4e ch.47 (Topical and intralesional chemotherapeutic agents); Khopkar (Miscellaneous agents); Khopkar ch.28; Wolverton 4e ch.47. Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
